+# Chen and Chen's Eulerian triangle parity positivity
+
+## Abstract
+
+For every integer step at most minus three, two-step propagation makes each positive even row strictly positive.
+
+**Definition 1.1 (The exact boundary and recursion).**
+
+$$\forall m: \mathbb{Z}, (\forall T: \mathbb{N} \to \left(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}\right), ((\operatorname{Source}\left(m, T\right)) \iff ((\forall n: \mathbb{N}, ((1 \leq n) \Rightarrow ((T\left(n, 1\right) = 1) \land (T\left(n, n\right) = 1)))) \land (\forall n: \mathbb{N}, (\forall k: \mathbb{N}, ((1 < k) \Rightarrow ((k < n) \Rightarrow (T\left(n, k\right) = (m \cdot ((n: \mathbb{Z}) - (k: \mathbb{Z})) + 1) \cdot T\left(n - 1, k - 1\right) + (m \cdot ((k: \mathbb{Z}) - 1) + 1) \cdot T\left(n - 1, k\right)))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.Source` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Xin Chen and Yudian Chen (2026). *OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666: negative-step Eulerian triangles*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A392664>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666 define T(n,1)=T(n,n)=1 for n>=1, and the displayed recursion for 1<k<n, with m=-3,-4,-5 respectively. All values are integers. Row zero and positions outside 1<=k<=n are unconstrained. Subtractions in the two coefficients are integer subtractions; predecessor indices use natural subtraction.
+
+**Definition 1.2 (Existence and universal nonnegativity).**
+
+$$\forall m: \mathbb{Z}, ((\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(m\right)) \iff ((\exists T: \mathbb{N} \to \left(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}\right), (\operatorname{Source}\left(m, T\right))) \land (\forall T: \mathbb{N} \to \left(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}\right), ((\operatorname{Source}\left(m, T\right)) \Rightarrow (\forall n: \mathbb{N}, ((1 \leq n) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{Even}\left(n\right)) \Rightarrow (\forall k: \mathbb{N}, ((1 \leq k) \Rightarrow ((k \leq n) \Rightarrow (0 \leq T\left(n, k\right))))))))))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.ParityPositivity` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Xin Chen and Yudian Chen (2026). *OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666: negative-step Eulerian triangles*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A392664>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+A solution exists, and every solution has nonnegative entries in each positive even row. Existence is constructed recursively in the row index with arbitrary zero values outside the prescribed triangle. The universal clause applies to every extension, independently of those choices.
+
+**Definition 1.3 (The three conjectures together).**
+
+$$(claim) \iff ((\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(-3\right)) \land ((\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(-4\right)) \land (\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(-5\right))))$$
+
+*Formalization.* `D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.claim` (`✓ std3`).
+
+*Citation.* Xin Chen and Yudian Chen (2026). *OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666: negative-step Eulerian triangles*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A392664>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+The conjunction retains each source parameter separately, including existence and the quantifier over every solution for each parameter.
+
+**Theorem 1.4 (Strict positivity for every integer r at least three).**
+
+$$\forall r: \mathbb{Z}, ((3 \leq r) \Rightarrow (\forall T: \mathbb{N} \to \left(\mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{Z}\right), ((\operatorname{Source}\left(-r, T\right)) \Rightarrow (\forall n: \mathbb{N}, ((1 \leq n) \Rightarrow ((\operatorname{Even}\left(n\right)) \Rightarrow (\forall k: \mathbb{N}, ((1 \leq k) \Rightarrow ((k \leq n) \Rightarrow (0 < T\left(n, k\right)))))))))))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.even_rows_positive` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Xin Chen and Yudian Chen (2026). *OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666: negative-step Eulerian triangles*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A392664>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Let U satisfy the source recursion with m=-r. Reflection follows by row induction because the two recurrence coefficients exchange under k -> n+1-k. Put x(n)=U(n,2). The recursion gives x(2)=1 and x(n+2)=(r-1)^2*x(n)+r*(r-2)*n+2-r^2 for n>=2. In particular x(4)=2*r*(r-3)+3>0. For n>=4 the forcing term is positive: it equals r*(r-2)*(n-4)+3*r*(r-3)+r+2. Thus the second column is positive at every even row, and reflection gives the penultimate column. From a positive even row, both coefficients are negative at every interior position of the next odd row, making its interior negative. At positions 3 through n of row n+2 both predecessors are negative, so both products are positive. The second and penultimate positions use the column argument; the two boundary positions equal one. Induction starts at row two.
+
+**Theorem 1.5 (The complete source conjunction).**
+
+$$(\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(-3\right)) \land ((\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(-4\right)) \land (\operatorname{ParityPositivity}\left(-5\right)))$$
+
+*Proof.* Machine-checked in Lean as `D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.result` (`✓ std3`). ∎
+
+*Resolves.* `Problems/chen-chen-step-m-eulerian-parity-positivity` (proved) by `D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.result`.
+

+
+*Source.* Repository-derived.
+
+*Acknowledgement.* Xin Chen and Yudian Chen (2026). *OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666: negative-step Eulerian triangles*. URL: <https://oeis.org/A392664>.
+
+*Commentary.*
+
+Apply the general positivity theorem at r=3,4,5 and weaken strict positivity to nonnegativity. The recursively constructed solution supplies existence for each parameter. No assumption about a finite prefix or about the signs of later rows is used.
+

+   generality: G
+   mirror-B: D5/B/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity
+   mirror-E: none(waiver:symbolic-proof-no-numeric-artifact)
+   anchors: []
+   utility: none
+   digest: Eulerian triangles with integer step at most minus three have positive even rows. -/
+
+import Mathlib.Algebra.Ring.Parity
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Linarith
+import Mathlib.Tactic.NormNum
+import Mathlib.Tactic.Ring
+
+/-! Two-step sign propagation for Chen and Chen's negative-step Eulerian triangles.
+
+The escape audit tracked by issue #24785 remains unresolved: the
+`even_rows_positive` registration is `IE-C050 ClosedTruthReadout` under
+`source.params`, and the `result` registration is `IE-C050 ClosedTruthReadout`
+under `source.unlinked_operand` with operand `Classical.choice`. These are
+unresolved audit bindings; no `declared_validated` status is claimed.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+namespace D5.S1.Recurrence.Algebraic.ChenChenParityPositivity
+
+/-- The boundary and interior recursion in OEIS A392664--A392666.
+Values outside the triangle, including row zero, are unconstrained. -/
+def Source (m : ℤ) (T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ) : Prop :=
+  (∀ n, 1 ≤ n → T n 1 = 1 ∧ T n n = 1) ∧
+  ∀ n k, 1 < k → k < n →
+    T n k = (m * ((n : ℤ) - (k : ℤ)) + 1) * T (n - 1) (k - 1) +
+      (m * ((k : ℤ) - 1) + 1) * T (n - 1) k
+
+/-- Existence together with the assertion about every solution, without
+fixing an extension outside the source's triangular domain. -/
+def ParityPositivity (m : ℤ) : Prop :=
+  (∃ T, Source m T) ∧
+    ∀ T, Source m T → ∀ n, 1 ≤ n → Even n →
+      ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ n → 0 ≤ T n k
+
+/-- The conjunction of the three source conjectures. -/
+def claim : Prop :=
+  ParityPositivity (-3) ∧ ParityPositivity (-4) ∧ ParityPositivity (-5)
+
+private def triangle (m : ℤ) : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ
+  | 0, _ => 0
+  | n + 1, k => if k = 1 ∨ k = n + 1 then 1 else
+      (m * ((n + 1 : ℕ) - (k : ℤ)) + 1) * triangle m n (k - 1) +
+        (m * ((k : ℤ) - 1) + 1) * triangle m n k
+
+private theorem source_exists (m : ℤ) : ∃ T, Source m T := by
+  refine ⟨triangle m, ?_, ?_⟩
+  · intro n hn
+    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : n ≠ 0)
+    simp [triangle]
+  · intro n k hk hkn
+    obtain ⟨n, rfl⟩ := Nat.exists_eq_succ_of_ne_zero (by omega : n ≠ 0)
+    simp [triangle, show k ≠ 1 by omega, show k ≠ n + 1 by omega]
+
+private theorem reflection {m : ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ} (h : Source m T)
+    (n k : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n) :
+    T n k = T n (n + 1 - k) := by
+  induction n using Nat.strong_induction_on generalizing k with
+  | h n ih =>
+    by_cases hl : k = 1
+    · subst k
+      simpa using (h.1 n hn).1.trans (h.1 n hn).2.symm
+    by_cases hr : k = n
+    · subst k
+      simpa using (h.1 n hn).2.trans (h.1 n hn).1.symm
+    have hn' : 1 ≤ n - 1 := by omega
+    have e₁ := ih (n - 1) (by omega) (k - 1) hn' (by omega) (by omega)
+    have e₂ := ih (n - 1) (by omega) k hn' hk (by omega)
+    have i₁ : n - 1 + 1 - (k - 1) = n + 1 - k := by omega
+    have i₂ : n - 1 + 1 - k = n + 1 - k - 1 := by omega
+    rw [i₁] at e₁
+    rw [i₂] at e₂
+    rw [h.2 n k (by omega) (by omega),
+      h.2 n (n + 1 - k) (by omega) (by omega), ← e₁, ← e₂]
+    have hc : ((n + 1 - k : ℕ) : ℤ) = (n : ℤ) + 1 - (k : ℤ) := by omega
+    rw [hc]
+    ring
+
+private theorem second_step {r : ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ} (h : Source (-r) T)
+    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
+    T (n + 1) 2 = 1 - r * ((n : ℤ) - 1) + (1 - r) * T n 2 := by
+  rw [h.2 (n + 1) 2 (by omega) (by omega)]
+  simp only [Nat.add_sub_cancel, Nat.reduceSub, Nat.cast_add, Nat.cast_one,
+    Nat.cast_ofNat, (h.1 n (by omega)).1]
+  ring
+
+/-- Eliminating the intervening row makes the boundary-column forcing positive. -/
+private theorem second_two_step {r : ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ} (h : Source (-r) T)
+    (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) :
+    T (n + 2) 2 = (r - 1) ^ 2 * T n 2 +
+      r * (r - 2) * (n : ℤ) + 2 - r ^ 2 := by
+  rw [show n + 2 = (n + 1) + 1 by omega, second_step h _ (by omega),
+    second_step h n hn]
+  push_cast
+  ring
+
+private theorem second_even_positive {r : ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ}
+    (hr : 3 ≤ r) (h : Source (-r) T) (q : ℕ) : 0 < T (2 * q + 2) 2 := by
+  induction q with
+  | zero => simpa using (show (0 : ℤ) < T 2 2 by rw [(h.1 2 (by omega)).2]; omega)
+  | succ q ih =>
+    rw [show 2 * (q + 1) + 2 = (2 * q + 2) + 2 by omega,
+      second_two_step h _ (by omega)]
+    by_cases hq : q = 0
+    · subst q
+      norm_num only [mul_zero, zero_add, Nat.cast_ofNat]
+      rw [(h.1 2 (by omega)).2]
+      nlinarith [mul_nonneg (show 0 ≤ r by omega) (show 0 ≤ r - 3 by omega)]
+    · have hn : (4 : ℤ) ≤ (2 * q + 2 : ℕ) := by omega
+      have hp : 0 ≤ r * (r - 2) := mul_nonneg (by omega) (by omega)
+      have hf := mul_nonneg hp (show 0 ≤ ((2 * q + 2 : ℕ) : ℤ) - 4 by omega)
+      have hs : 0 < (r - 1) ^ 2 * T (2 * q + 2) 2 :=
+        mul_pos (sq_pos_of_pos (by omega)) ih
+      nlinarith [mul_nonneg (show 0 ≤ r by omega) (show 0 ≤ r - 3 by omega)]
+
+private theorem coefficient_negative {r : ℤ} (hr : 3 ≤ r) {a : ℤ} (ha : 1 ≤ a) :
+    -r * a + 1 < 0 := by
+  have := mul_nonneg (show 0 ≤ r by omega) (show 0 ≤ a - 1 by omega)
+  nlinarith
+
+private theorem next_interior_negative {r : ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ}
+    (hr : 3 ≤ r) (h : Source (-r) T) (n : ℕ)
+    (hp : ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ n → 0 < T n k)
+    (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 < k) (hkn : k < n + 1) : T (n + 1) k < 0 := by
+  rw [h.2 (n + 1) k hk hkn, Nat.add_sub_cancel]
+  exact add_neg
+    (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (coefficient_negative hr (by omega)) (hp _ (by omega) (by omega)))
+    (mul_neg_of_neg_of_pos (coefficient_negative hr (by omega)) (hp _ (by omega) (by omega)))
+
+private theorem positive_rows {r : ℤ} {T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ}
+    (hr : 3 ≤ r) (h : Source (-r) T) (q : ℕ) :
+    ∀ k, 1 ≤ k → k ≤ 2 * q + 2 → 0 < T (2 * q + 2) k := by
+  induction q with
+  | zero =>
+    intro k hk hkn
+    have : k = 1 ∨ k = 2 := by omega
+    rcases this with rfl | rfl <;> norm_num [(h.1 2 (by omega)).1, (h.1 2 (by omega)).2]
+  | succ q ih =>
+    intro k hk hkn
+    by_cases hl : k = 1
+    · subst k
+      rw [(h.1 _ (by omega)).1]
+      omega
+    by_cases hr' : k = 2 * (q + 1) + 2
+    · subst k
+      rw [(h.1 _ (by omega)).2]
+      omega
+    by_cases hs : k = 2
+    · subst k
+      exact second_even_positive hr h (q + 1)
+    by_cases ht : k = 2 * (q + 1) + 1
+    · rw [reflection h _ k (by omega) hk hkn]
+      have : 2 * (q + 1) + 2 + 1 - k = 2 := by omega
+      rw [this]
+      exact second_even_positive hr h (q + 1)
+    have hn₁ := next_interior_negative hr h (2 * q + 2) ih
+      (k - 1) (by omega) (by omega)
+    have hn₂ := next_interior_negative hr h (2 * q + 2) ih
+      k (by omega) (by omega)
+    rw [h.2 _ k (by omega) (by omega)]
+    have hi : 2 * (q + 1) + 2 - 1 = 2 * q + 2 + 1 := by omega
+    rw [hi]
+    exact add_pos
+      (mul_pos_of_neg_of_neg (coefficient_negative hr (by omega)) hn₁)
+      (mul_pos_of_neg_of_neg (coefficient_negative hr (by omega)) hn₂)
+
+/-- Every admissible triangle for an integer step -r, r ≥ 3, has strictly
+positive entries throughout each positive even row. -/
+theorem even_rows_positive (r : ℤ) (hr : 3 ≤ r) (T : ℕ → ℕ → ℤ)
+    (h : Source (-r) T) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (he : Even n)
+    (k : ℕ) (hk : 1 ≤ k) (hkn : k ≤ n) : 0 < T n k := by
+  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := he
+  have hq' : 1 ≤ q := by omega
+  have hn' : n = 2 * (q - 1) + 2 := by omega
+  rw [hn']
+  exact positive_rows hr h (q - 1) k hk (by omega)
+
+private theorem parameter_claim (r : ℤ) (hr : 3 ≤ r) : ParityPositivity (-r) := by
+  refine ⟨source_exists _, ?_⟩
+  intro T h n hn he k hk hkn
+  exact le_of_lt (even_rows_positive r hr T h n hn he k hk hkn)
+
+/-- The three original nonnegativity assertions, including existence and the
+universal quantifier over all solutions of each source recurrence. -/
+theorem result : claim := by
+  exact ⟨parameter_claim 3 (by omega), parameter_claim 4 (by omega),
+    parameter_claim 5 (by omega)⟩
+
+#print axioms even_rows_positive
+#print axioms result
+
+end D5.S1.Recurrence.Algebraic.ChenChenParityPositivity

+---
+slug: chen-chen-step-m-eulerian-parity-positivity
+bibkey: chenchen2026stepm

+
+# Chen and Chen's step-m Eulerian parity positivity
+
+## Problem
+
+For each m=-3,-4,-5, let T map pairs of natural numbers to integers, with
+T(n,1)=T(n,n)=1 for n>=1 and
+
+`T(n,k)=(m*(n-k)+1)*T(n-1,k-1)+(m*(k-1)+1)*T(n-1,k)`
+
+for 1<k<n. The conjectures in OEIS A392664, A392665 and A392666 assert
+T(n,k)>=0 for every positive even n and every 1<=k<=n. The exact Lean
+`claim` conjoins, for each parameter, existence of a solution and this
+assertion for every solution. Row zero and entries outside the triangle
+are unconstrained, and no uniqueness of the total extension is assumed.
+
+## Motivation
+
+This is the conjunction scoped by
+[#24785](https://github.com/the-omega-institute/trureturing/issues/24785).
+The finite verification through row 400 in the source does not prove the
+unbounded claim. The stronger mathematical target uses every integer r>=3
+and m=-r, and proves strictly positive even rows.
+
+## Gap
+
+The three directly read OEIS internal pages label the nonnegativity
+assertion a conjecture. Repository and pinned Mathlib searches for the
+identifiers and step-m Eulerian recursion found no exact prior theorem.
+Mathlib supplies integer order, parity and induction; the row recursion
+and its sign estimates are the source-specific part. arXiv API identifier
+search for the disjunction of A392664, A392665 and A392666 returned zero
+records. The structural query `Eulerian AND triangle AND positivity`
+returned nine records, including arXiv:2007.12602, arXiv:2012.03629 and
+arXiv:2608.29224. Their abstracts discuss generalized Eulerian triangles
+and positivity; full-text comparison of their hypotheses with the
+negative-step source remains unverified. Public GitHub repository search
+for A392664 returned zero repositories. GitHub code
+search required authentication, so that search is incomplete. No global
+absence or priority claim follows from these bounded searches.
+
+## Route
+
+Construct a total solution recursively in the row index. Prove reflection
+T(n,k)=T(n,n+1-k) by strong induction, using only triangular positions.
+
+For m=-r and x(n)=T(n,2), eliminate the intervening row to obtain
+
+`x(n+2)=(r-1)^2*x(n)+r*(r-2)*n+2-r^2` for n>=2.
+
+The initial values are x(2)=1 and x(4)=2*r*(r-3)+3. For n>=4 the
+forcing term equals
+
+`r*(r-2)*(n-4)+3*r*(r-3)+r+2`,
+
+which is positive for r>=3. Thus all even second-column values are
+positive, and reflection supplies the penultimate column. From a
+positive even row n, the negative recurrence coefficients make every
+interior entry in row n+1 negative. At positions 3<=k<=n of row n+2,
+both predecessors are negative and both products are positive. The
+second and penultimate columns are treated by the independent column
+argument, and the boundary values equal one. Induction from row two
+gives strict positivity throughout every positive even row.
+
+Specializing the one general theorem at r=3,4,5 and adjoining the
+constructed existence witnesses gives the exact source conjunction.
+The parameter threshold cannot include r=2: the literal recursion then
+forces T(3,2)=-2 and T(4,2)=-1.
+
+## Falsifier
+
+A solution of one of the three literal recursions with a negative entry
+at a positive even row and a column between one and that row would
+refute the source claim. A disagreement outside the prescribed triangle
+would not. Finite positive prefixes cannot establish the result.
+
+## Evidence
+
+The Lean owner is
+`D5/S1/Recurrence/Algebraic/ChenChenParityPositivity.lean`.
+The generic theorem is `even_rows_positive`; `result` states the entire
+`claim`, including both existence and universality at each parameter.
+
+## Triage
+
+The general theorem has `proof_shape: content` and admission basis
